findings.detail: Design integrates cleanly with existing A2A/SSE/ACP architecture. No infrastructure conflicts. Three-layer approach (prompt layer → guideline layer → gate layer) builds on existing components: InputRequiredReason enum (no new values needed), A2A PATCH input-required handoff (existing SSE → watchdog → Reviewer routing), ACP session/fork from Manager (existing agent_working.py with UPDATE ONLY constraint), and the freely-review entry point. Key unresolved gaps (identified in the design itself): (a) agent_working.py schema lacks review_verdict/review_stage/reviewed_by/reviewed_at/review_findings fields — planned addition but not yet present; (b) freely-review currently exits 0 silently when ACP unavailable, design correctly flags this as needing change; (c) cross-model enforcement is warning-only (acknowledged trade-off, not a blocking issue at B1).

All 5 phases (B1/B2/RED/dev/GREEN) have clear, explicit completion signals in their phase-definitions: (B1) brainstorms.md + candidates.md + milestones.md candidate_issues with candidate promoted; (B2) I-* phase_state=done_b2_ibm + pre-tests.md + tasks.md + IDN; (RED) all AT red-green-status=red + actual_RED_output real + bug confirmed; (Dev) all AT code implemented + tasks done + code committed; (GREEN) all AT red-green-status=green + actual_output real + TEST_STATUS=completed. Each definition ends with '调用 A2A PATCH state=input-required, reason=needs-review:{phase}' — same consistent handoff mechanism across all phases. The A2A PATCH input-required mechanism is the correct choice: it's already defined in InputRequiredReason, routed by watchdog_sse.py, and supports session/fork from Manager. Key concern: Worker still holds trigger authority — no runtime enforcement at phase transition boundary. The design consciously accepts this, relying on the command-layer gate (pr-create-guarded review signature check) as hard fallback. This is valid but a 'late catch' — Worker could skip reviews across multiple phases before PR-time enforcement. Brainstorms.md correctly identifies this root problem and the three-layer mitigation.

All 5 phase-definitions and their corresponding review-guidelines are well-aligned. Each phase-definition's completion criteria map directly to review-guideline check items: (B1) root cause analysis ↔ solution exploration ↔ candidate digestion ↔ document completeness; (B2) I-* issue completeness ↔ PRD quality ↔ pre-tests coverage; (RED) RED execution authenticity ↔ RED consistency ↔ coverage completeness; (Dev) TDD fidelity ↔ PRD fidelity ↔ tasks completeness ↔ IDN; (GREEN) all green ↔ evidence authenticity ↔ no ghost pass ↔ test-gate.env. Observation: green.md uses needs-review:test rather than needs-review:green, and the enum value is NEEDS_REVIEW_TEST — this is functionally consistent (the enum value is what matters for routing), just a name asymmetry between the phase label 'GREEN' and the enum 'test'. All B1 output files verified: brainstorms.md (exists, complete with Discovery/Problem/Brainstorm/Decision), candidates.md (exists, all fields present including acceptance_criteria/promotion_gate/decision_reason), milestones.md (M-20260707T113841Z-A entry with C-20260707T113841Z-A under candidate_issues, status=promoted).

summary: B1 design PASS. The proposal correctly identifies the systemic gap in review enforcement (Worker controls review trigger, no hard fallback) and proposes a sound three-layer solution that integrates cleanly with existing A2A/SSE/ACP infrastructure. Phase-definitions and review-guidelines are symmetric and well-aligned. The core trade-off (relying on command-layer gate as late enforcement) is acknowledged and justifiable given existing architecture constraints. Implementation gaps (agent_working schema, freely-review fix, pr-create-guarded gate chain) are explicitly identified as B2/dev scope.
